title: Puni Jump
duplicate_check: No matching host in prior-urls.json, catalog-baseline.json published_games, or previously_seen_urls.
controls_actions: Read How to play: left/right to jump in that direction; holding makes the jump higher; stomp enemies from above; jump again immediately after a stomp for combos; wall-jump by sliding and tapping toward a wall.
Turned sound off before play; the control changed to “Turn sound on” (Value 0).
Tapped Let’s jump! and entered Stage 01 with 3 lives and a 30-second timer.
Clicked the right control, then pressed Left. The mushroom avatar moved across the playfield and the game displayed NICE SLIP!
gameplay_outcome: Actual directional movement and a near-miss event were observed. The test timer expired before scoring; HUD remained at 3 lives and score 000. Gameplay response is verified, but this was a short control sample rather than a completed stage.
mechanics: Portrait arcade platformer: direct the mushroom to jump through a vertical field, stomp spiky enemies, chain jumps for score, and avoid losing lives.
visual_art: Minimal pastel, hand-drawn style with an orange mushroom protagonist, simple clouds and rolling hills, and expressive spiky enemies.
existing_custom_cover_evidence: The live title screen includes a custom PUNI JUMP wordmark and mushroom character; no separate promotional cover asset was verified.
thumbnail_concepts: Text-free, low-angle action shot of the orange mushroom springing high above a spiky enemy, with a tall pastel sky to sell the vertical jump.
The mushroom narrowly dodging a cluster of spiky enemies mid-air, with the pastel hill and cloud backdrop and clear protagonist silhouette.
screenshot_note: Gameplay screenshots were captured and shown inline in the CUA tool output; this subagent CUA surface exposes no supported local screenshot-file export, so no path was saved.
audio: The in-game control changed to “Turn sound on” (Value 0) before starting. This is not proof of browser-level muting. All test tabs were closed immediately when parent reported the user still heard audio; no further testing.
